summary: The causal attribution, the choice of recoverV3LiveReplica() as the sole reconciliation owner, the no-new-marker/schema/API conclusion, and the choke-point placement of the fold recheck in stageClosedBlueprintEpoch() are all correct and verified against source: only recoverV3LiveReplica() mints a RecoveredV3Live capability (v3-live.ts:5322), so a fresh registration with a clear flag genuinely requires the authenticated outbox/journal scan (v3-live.ts:5155-5199), and stageBlueprintEpoch() sets blueprintClosing synchronously and queues the fold behind the in-flight issue (v3-live.ts:6713-6714), making the fold-time recheck sufficient for both bind orderings on the paths the plan names. One blocking gap remains: the freeze scopes GREEN to committedFailure() only, but issuer.issue() can also *reject* after the durable commit — the genuine node store COMMITs (node-issuance-store.ts:802) and then throws UnknownOutcomeFailure from its readback (terminal.ts:126) — and that arm (v3-live.ts:5682-5699) still marks recovery-required only when an operation-policy reservation exists, which is precisely the no-policy configuration GREEN step 1 exists to fix. An implementation matching the freeze would satisfy the frozen acceptance while the demonstrated defect survives under that ordering, which is also absent from the fault matrix. RED is causal and feasible as written; two P2s are dispositioned to the implementation owner.

findings.title: Post-commit issuer.issue() rejection is outside the frozen GREEN, so the defect survives with no policy installed
findings.evidence: Plan lines 96239-96248 scope step 1 to "after issuer.issue() returned, every committedFailure()"; audit.md:9-13 asserts "All failures from committedFailure() therefore occur after durable issuance". But packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:5682-5699 is a second post-durable arm: node-issuance-store.ts:802 executes COMMIT, then line 819 calls #classifyAfterTerminalSuppression(); if the readback fails (lines 829-838 -> observation {unreadable:true}) packages/issuance-store/src/terminal.ts:126 throws UnknownOutcomeFailure, so transactIssue() rejects after the issued+outbox rows are durably committed. In that arm v3-live.ts:5685-5687 sets operationAdmissionHalted only when `reservation !== undefined`, and reserveOperation() returns undefined whenever no policy is installed (v3-live.ts:4150). For a non-terminal issue terminalTransactionStarted is false, so line 5698 returns admission-rejected with the flag clear. The frozen fault matrix (plan lines 96294-96298) lists "journal write then thrown outcome" but no issuance-transaction-rejects-after-commit ordering.
findings.impact: In a deployment with no operation admission policy - exactly the configuration step 1 is written to cover - a durably committed issued/pending-outbox row leaves operationAdmissionHalted false, so neither the bind-time refusal (step 2) nor the queued fold recheck (step 3) fires. creatorCloseRegistration() mints close authority and stageClosedBlueprintEpoch() folds a graph omitting the row, reproducing the demonstrated defect; after adoption that row still carries the old epoch/anchor and freezes later closes with D110C_0C1A_RETIREMENT_CHECKPOINT_UNAVAILABLE. Because the ordering is not in the acceptance matrix, an incomplete GREEN passes.
findings.required_action: Extend GREEN step 1 from "every committedFailure()" to "every failure that is not provably pre-durable": at v3-live.ts:5685-5687 drop only the `reservation !== undefined` condition, keeping the existing `!signerResolved && !terminalTransactionStarted` release discriminator so the retained E5-01 gate "releases a definitely pre-issuance failure and permits one clean retry" (tests/e5-01-v3-operation-admission-red.test.ts:172-204, signer rejects before resolving) stays green. Add one fault case to the RED/GREEN matrix: the issuance transaction rejects with an unknown outcome after its durable commit, with no operation admission policy installed, and the close must still refuse. No schema, API, wire field, or store change is implied.

findings.title: Reusing operationAdmissionHalted widens the halt and refusal domain beyond local issuance without acceptance coverage
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3727 refuses every non-duplicate received vertex while the flag is set, and the ingress path itself sets the same flag at lines 3803, 3813, 3827, 3834, 3840 and 3853. Unconditional marking therefore newly halts gossip admission in no-policy deployments after a post-commit local-issue failure, and conversely a received-vertex journal/graph failure will now refuse creator close under steps 2 and 3. The frozen acceptance (plan lines 96281-96292) states only that neither refusal may change durable head, snapshot, graph, application state, or the surviving row.
findings.impact: A behavior change outside the stated close-refusal scope ships unstated: an ingress-side halt can block a close that would previously have proceeded, and a local post-commit failure now stops received-vertex admission. Both are fail-closed and defensible, but they are untested and could surface as an unexplained retained-gate failure at GREEN.
findings.required_action: Owner: D.110c-0c1b implementation. State both consequences explicitly in the acceptance text and pin them with one assertion in the retained D.110c-a/b hot path (a plane with no injected failure still binds and closes). No executable scope change beyond that assertion.

findings.title: blueprintClosing stays latched after a step-3 fold refusal and is not covered by the refusal-state assertions
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6713 sets registration.blueprintClosing = true synchronously before the fold is queued at 6714; a step-3 recheck failure returns a fold failure and stageSnapshot() maps it to snapshotExportFailure (7029) without resetting the flag. issueLocal() (5842) and authenticateV3Ingress() (3888) then refuse for the life of the registration, and only abortSnapshotStage() (6991-6996) clears it.
findings.impact: After a correct refusal the plane is left latched closed in memory. This is harmless under the plan's deactivate-then-recover remedy, but the frozen acceptance does not assert the post-refusal in-memory state, so either behavior (latched or reset) would pass and the eventual choice is unrecorded.
findings.required_action: Owner: D.110c-0c1b implementation. Assert the intended post-refusal registration state in GREEN - either the refusal leaves blueprintClosing latched and recovery is the only exit, or step 3 resets it - and record the choice in the plan text. No new product surface.
